# VIETNAM THERMAL POWER GENERATION INVENTORY (>30 MWe)

**Report Date:** 23 May 2026
**Analyst Methodology:** Primary-sourced inventory based on Vietnamese government documents (PDP8/Decision 500/QĐ-TTg, Amended PDP8/Decision 768/QĐ-TTg), EVN and PVN filings, operator (PV Power, EVNGENCO) press releases, supplemented by Global Energy Monitor Coal Plant Tracker (Jan 2026 release) and trade press.

---

## 1. Sector Overview

Vietnam's electricity system had an estimated total installed capacity exceeding 80 GW by end-2025, of which thermal generation (coal, gas, oil) represents roughly 45–50%.

citations.cited_text: The agreement proposed reducing Vietnam’s coal fleet capacity from 37 GW to 30.2 GW by 2030 and a path to “phasing out unabated coal-fired power gener...
citations.title: Na Duong power station - Global Energy Monitor

content.text: As of January 2023, the Global Coal Plant Tracker estimated Vietnam had 24.7 GW in coal capacity, with a further 6.1 GW under construction.

Domestic gas-fired capacity adds approximately 7–8 GW, concentrated in the Phú Mỹ complex (Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu), Cà Mau, Nhơn Trạch (Đồng Nai), and Ô Môn (Cần Thơ).

**Policy Framework — PDP8 and Amendments:** The Eighth Power Development Plan (Quy hoạch Điện VIII, Decision 500/QĐ-TTg, May 2023) capped coal at ~30.1 GW by 2030, restricted to projects already under construction, and set an ambitious LNG target of 22,400 MW. The Amended PDP8 (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, April 2025) modestly raised the LNG ceiling to 22,524 MW while deferring Long Sơn and Long An II LNG projects to 2031–2035. The JETP agreement (December 2022) committed Vietnam to reducing coal fleet capacity from 37 GW to 30.2 GW by 2030.

**Key Actors:**
- **EVN** (Vietnam Electricity): State-owned utility; operates through EVNGENCO1, EVNGENCO2, EVNGENCO3
- **PVN** (Petrovietnam/Vietnam National Industry-Energy Group): Parent of PV Power; owns coal (Thái Bình 2, Sông Hậu 1, Long Phú 1) and gas/LNG assets
- **TKV** (Vinacomin): Coal mining SOE; operates mine-mouth coal plants (Na Dương, Cao Ngạn, Cẩm Phả, Sơn Động, Mạo Khê)
- **BOT investors**: AES (Mông Dương 2), Marubeni/KEPCO (Nghi Sơn 2), Mitsubishi/KEPCO (Vũng Áng 2), Sumitomo/JERA (Vân Phong 1), COPI/China (Vĩnh Tân 1), Jaks/CECI (Hải Dương)
- **MOIT**: Ministry of Industry and Trade; regulatory oversight

**Challenges:** Coal phase-down under JETP commitments vs. demand growth (~12–15% per annum for sustained GDP growth); LNG transition hampered by infrastructure delays (only 3 of 13 PDP8 LNG projects on schedule); Long Phú 1 stalled by Russian sanctions; renewable integration causing curtailment but insufficient baseload replacement.
